mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 0.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below -0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST and a fall in GDPC1 over two months indicates a shift from broad economic growth to housing-specific demand, which historically precedes underperformance of S&P 500 due to sector rotation, resulting in negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between PAYEMS rising above 0.3% monthly and UNRATE above 7% for two months signals an overheating labor market, which increases inflationary pressure and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as central banks respond with tightening.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent low FEDFUNDS rate below 1% for more than one year, combined with a stable CPIAUCSL, indicates a prolonged accommodative monetary policy environment that supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for > 12 months and |CPIAUCSL change| < 0.5% over last 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in RSAFS above 2% for four consecutive months signals robust retail sales growth, which typically precedes positive consumer confidence and higher corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
